Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will have the option to use an alternative version of the "App Tracking Transparency" system prompt in the EU, as part of an agreement Apple reached with the bloc earlier. Here are the details.

New prompt mandatory in select European countries

Apple confirmed several weeks ago that it would comply with the EU's "more equitable" App Tracking Transparency rules, after Germany's Federal Cartel Office opened an investigation into the matter.

The agreement ends a years-long antitrust investigation into whether Apple's ATT rules placed third-party apps at an unfair competitive disadvantage relative to Apple's own services. Apple has consistently denied the allegations, claiming it applies equally strict privacy principles from the ground up to its own apps. German regulators, however, have remained unconvinced by that argument.

As a result, Apple agreed to make eight adjustments to its ATT framework in Europe, which you can read more about here.

Apple today confirmed that iOS 27 will allow developers to choose whether or not to "use an alternative version of the App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU," adding that "based on legal requirements, apps distributed in Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and Romania may only use the alternative version of the system prompt."

In an updated "User privacy and data use" developer support page, Apple further detailed what the alternative version of the system prompt will entail:

The company further noted that EU developers will also be able to re-prompt users one year after their last ATT choice, regardless of whether they originally accepted or declined tracking.
